sentences.text: Megasphaera elsdenii is a prominent lactate consumer in the rumen of livestock, and in humans it can be isolated from faeces of healthy donors and of patients with inflammatory conditions.
A comparison of 86 M. elsdenii genomes from human faeces with animal gut isolates reported that human and animal lineages intermingle without host-specific clustering.
Another study identified Megasphaera as an infrequent, low-abundance taxon contributing to lactose- and lactate-driven production of the short-chain acid valerate in overweight and obese women.
In the vagina, two taxa grouped within the genus Megasphaera, phylotypes 1 and 2, have been previously associated with bacterial vaginosis and pregnancy complications.
